task: Na/K-ATPase + membrane ion transport CERT: (1) pump stoichiometry 3Na+ out/2K+ in per ATP, electrogenic; (2) Nernst/Goldman-Hodgkin-Katz resting membrane potential from measured ion concentrations + permeability ratios (PK:PNa:PCl ~1:0.04:0.45) reproducing ~-70mV neuron / ~-90mV muscle; (3) pump turnover rate ~100-150/s per pump, ~8000 pumps/cell scale; (4) Na/K-ATPase share of cellular ATP budget ~20-40% of basal metabolic rate (higher neurons/kidney). Decorrelated check: electrogenic contribution ~-5 to -15mV distinct from the Goldman diffusion potential (ouabain-sensitive).
confidence_tier: in-vitro/in-vivo-anchored (patch-clamp/flame-photometry Vm measurements, ouabain-sensitive respirometry, radioisotope-occlusion enzyme kinetics, 3H-ouabain-binding site density) -- per the task's own framing. NOT upgraded to a higher tier: several founding papers (Hodgkin-Katz 1949, Hodgkin-Horowicz 1959, Whittam 1962, Thomas 1972) had publisher-blocked full text this session, so their SPECIFIC in-text numbers are not independently re-extracted here; modern papers that verbatim-quantify the same phenomena carry the numeric weight instead (see citations below).

symmetric_qc_open_items: Permeability ratio 1:0.04:0.45's own single-paper provenance not traced live this session (WebSearch budget exhausted mid-session, disclosed not hidden) -- tested AS GIVEN per the task's framing rather than re-derived.

Turnover convergence (G3) is Q10=2.0-dependent and has a genuine unit-interpretation ambiguity in the Karlish & Stein 1982 source (ion-count vs cycle-rate) -- both disclosed with the sensitivity table in the script output.

ATP-budget global figure (13.7-20.2% of total O2) sits BELOW the task's stated 20-40% floor at its low end, touching it only at its ceiling -- the flat 20-40% band is better supported by kidney/brain-specific figures than as a whole-body average.
Electrogenic contribution real spread (8.4-24mV) runs at/above the task's 5-15mV band, not comfortably inside it.

Pump density spread (285 to 5.45x10^6/cell, 19,123-fold) brackets the task's ~8000/cell anchor but no live source matches it closely; also flagged that 'pumps per cell' is itself geometry-dependent (a giant skeletal-muscle fiber's areal density implies ~10^10 pumps/fiber).

Lipicky et al 1971's back-calculated intracellular Na/Cl (83.7/79.4 mEq/L) are far above idealized frog-muscle textbook figures -- plausibly a real feature of the dissected human ex-vivo prep, not re-verified against a second independent human dataset this session.
